author: seejayhess
text:
I think too many people see AI labs as just the models.

The model matters, obviously. But the better question is who controls the stuff around it: compute, power, data, distribution, products people use, government relationships, and the ability to wire all of that together without lighting the company on fire.

At some point the model starts to look like the UI for the utility underneath.

So unfortunately, I have to talk about Factorio.

If you’ve never played Factorio, it’s just Minecraft for people who think the fun part is supply chains. You crash on a planet, mine rocks, build machines to mine, build machines to build, and eventually build the factory that builds factories.

The game is bottlenecks. You fix iron, then power breaks. You fix power, then throughput breaks. You fix throughput, then some tiny thing three screens away is starving the whole factory.

That is the AI race now.

So, rough map of the factory floor.

1/ OpenAI has the default app. ChatGPT was the first real AI product people used, and when someone says AI, a lot of them still mean ChatGPT. Monster advantage. The problem is the factory still depends on someone else’s infrastructure, particularly Microsoft. Stargate is the attempt to own more of the power bill, but it can also become partner spaghetti around one insane product.

2/ Anthropic has taste. Claude is still the model I trust most when the work requires taste instead of horsepower: intent understanding, steerability, the feeling that it wants to work with you. But trust does not magically buy power. The model serious teams trust can still get outscaled by someone with a wider resource base.

Also, the Fable mess was a reminder that government is now part of the game, not adjacent to it.

3/ Google should be absolutely destroying this. They have TPUs, Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Gmail, Docs, Cloud, distribution to billions of humans, and more data than anyone wants to admit. If Gemini, Workspace, Search, Cloud, YouTube, and dev tools ever feed the same system, everyone should be terrified. If not, every keynote stays a little bit “wait, which product is this in again?”

4/ Meta, Meta, Meta. With Llama, Meta is trying to make its defaults everyone’s defaults. In open source, defaults are power. The play is probably smart: give everyone the ecosystem, keep the sharpest edge for yourself, and hope open source doesn’t commoditize the thing you’re trying to win. Very Zuck, and probably underrated.

5/ xAI and Elon are where this gets messy. The obvious take is “Grok is behind, therefore xAI is behind.” Maybe, if this is only a chatbot race. But if the AI race is Factorio, Grok might be the wrong thing to judge. X gives him messy human feedback and distribution, Tesla gives him cars, batteries, factories, robots, and a path to embodiment, SpaceX gives him satellites, defense relevance, and government relationships, Colossus gives him data-center execution, and xAI gives him the model. None of this automatically composes, and because it is Elon the factory might just be five burning factories in a trench coat. But if it does compose, the upside is not “Grok gets a little better.” It is that the weird pieces start feeding each other.

That is not a chatbot company. That is a factory.

Soooo just Factorio.

The smartest model matters. It’s just not the whole game...just like Factorio

author: johnnys_dream
text:
2026年6月にAnthropicが発表した最上位のMythos 5およびFable 5を巡るドタバタ劇と、Zhipu AIのGLM-5.2などの中華オープンソース（OS）モデルの台頭は、この米欧企業の中華シフト・OSシフトの引き金になりつつある。

AnthropicはFable 5でサイバーセキュリティや生物学などのトピックを厳しく制限し、拒否されたらOpus 4.8にフォールバックさせる仕様にしたが、ビジネスでガンガン使いたい企業からすれば金を払っているのに思い通りにいかないストレスが溜まっている。

さらに最悪だったのが、2026年6月中旬、米政府の輸出管理指令によってFable 5 / Mythos 5へのアクセスが突然グローバルで強制停止された事件だ（後に一部米企業向けに解除）。これにより企業は、

「米国のクラウドAPIに依存していると、政府の一言で明日ビジネスが止まる」

という強烈な地政学リスクを植え付けられた。その点、GLM-5.2などのオープンモデルをローカルや自社クラウドにダウンロードしてしまえば、文字通り誰にも遮断できない最強の聖域が手に入る。

Fable 5のAPI価格は『入力$10 / 出力$50（100万トークンあたり）』と非常に高価だ。さらに、非常に優秀だと話題になった開発ツールのClaude Codeも、定額サブスクからヘビーな従量課金制へと移行したため、開発者が一日中コードを回すと絶望的なコストに跳ね上がる無理ゲー状態になった。

一方で、中華OSモデル（GLM-5.2やDeepSeekの系譜）は、商用利用可能な上にFableやOpenAIの最新鋭に肉薄するエージェント能力・コーディング能力を持ちながら、APIコストは5分の1〜6分の1という圧倒的なコスパを実現している。自社サーバーで回せば、電気代とハードウェア代だけで叩き放題だ。

加えて、Anthropicは不正利用監視のために30日間データを保存するとポリシーに明記している。企業の機密コードや顧客データを扱う側からすれば、この30日間人質に取られる状態はガバナンスの観点からアウトになるケースが多い。

手元で生モデルを動かせば、データは外に出ない。さらに、その自社データを使ってローカルで微調整や追加学習を施し、自社業務に特化した最強のオレオレモデルへ育成できるアドバンテージは、APIで叩くだけのクローズドモデルには真似できない。

米国側が自国の先端AIを止めれば中国や世界は困るだろうと高を括っていたら、市場はさっさと実用的で、安くて、規制されない中華OSやローカル運用に流れてしまっている。

正しさや安全を大義名分にユーザーに不便を強いる米大手AIに対し、安さ・実用性・自由で殴り込みをかける中華OSモデル。ビジネスの現場がどちらを選ぶかは、思想云々ではなく純粋な経済合理性の結果になるだろう。

こうした流れの中で日本企業が取るべき現実的な戦略は、

①重要業務にはAPI依存を減らす（特に米国製閉鎖モデル）

②GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek系をオンプレまたは国内クラウドにデプロイ

③自社データでファインチューニングし、業界特化型AIを構築

④米国製APIは補助的に使い、メインはオープンモデルで構成

になるのではないか。

中華OSモデルはEU・東南アジア・中東からも採用が拡大している。この流れは一時的なブームではなく、構造的なシフトだ。日本企業も米国最先端AI信仰から脱却し、マルチモデル＋オープンソース・ローカル運用を前提としたアーキテクチャへ移行すべき時期に来ている。

「最も賢いモデルを、全てのタスクに使う必要はない」

生成AIが当たり前になるほど、静かに膨らんでいくのが『トークンコスト』です。米Gartnerによれば、AIインフラの効率化でモデル単価そのものは下がっていく一方、チャット型AIの5〜30倍ものトークンを消費するAIエージェントの普及によって、企業が支払う推論の総コストはむしろ増えていく見通しとのこと。「安くなったはずなのに、請求額は増えている」という逆転現象です。

日本でも帝国データバンクの調査では、小規模企業を中心にAIのコスト負担が課題として挙がりもはや『経営課題』として認識され始めています。

ではどう抑えるか。Anthropicの「Claude Platform」担当のアンジェラ・ジャン氏とケイトリン・レス氏が、実践的な2つの手法を語っていたので整理してみます📝

■ 手法1：AIを「先生と生徒」に分ける
ひとつ目は『アドバイザー戦略』。高性能モデルを「アドバイザー（先生）」、安価なモデルを「エグゼキューター（生徒）」として組み合わせる手法です。
・基本は安いモデルが作業を実行
・判断に迷ったときだけ、高性能モデルに助言を求める
・結果として、安価なモデル単体よりも高い精度を実現

レス氏いわく「アドバイザー戦略を使えば、最先端モデル相当の性能をはるかに安く実現できる」とのこと。肝は、タスクの難易度に応じて段階的に組み合わせることです。

・最難関：Fable 5（先生）×Opus（生徒）
・中程度：Opus（先生）×Sonnet（生徒）
・軽い処理：Sonnet×Haiku 4.5

ここでいう「難しい問題」とは、大規模なレガシーシステムの移行、膨大なデータ処理、影響範囲の広い脆弱性調査、ゲーム開発のような工程の多い案件などを指すそうです。いずれもSIerの現場が日々向き合っているテーマばかり。なお、最上位モデルをアドバイザーに据えれば、実行役が下位モデルでも長時間タスクの処理能力は維持される、という説明も印象的でした。

■ 手法2：プロンプトキャッシングで賢く入力する
ふたつ目は『プロンプトキャッシング』。システムプロンプトやツール指定、メッセージ履歴など、リクエストの冒頭で毎回繰り返す部分をキャッシュし、再処理コストを省く仕組みです。

具体的な料金感は次の通り。
・Opus 4.8の通常入力：100万トークンあたり10ドル
・キャッシュ書き込み（5分保持）：6.25ドル
・キャッシュヒット（2回目以降）：わずか0.5ドル
初回こそ書き込みの追加料金がかかるものの、2回目以降は通常入力の20分の1。社内規定を毎回参照する問い合わせbotや、同じ長文ドキュメントを扱うシステムのように「冒頭が毎回同じ」用途ほど、効果は跳ね上がります。

デフォルトの保持時間は5分ですが、追加料金で1時間まで延ばせるため、アクセスが断続的に続くサービスとも相性が良さそうです。先のアドバイザー戦略と組み合わせれば、削減効果はさらに積み上がります。

ここまで整理して感じたのは、これはまさにSIerや社内開発の腕の見せどころだということ。

「とりあえず一番強いモデルで」という発想は、もはやコスト面で通用しません。求められるのは、業務フローをタスク単位に分解し、それぞれの難易度に最適なモデルを割り当てる『設計力』です。そしてこの設計力こそ、これまでシステムのアーキテクチャを描いてきたエンジニアが最も得意とするところ。SIerにとっては「AI導入で仕事が消える」どころか、コスト設計という新しい付加価値を提案できる好機とも言えます。

つまりAIコストの最適化は、単なる節約術ではなく、設計力がそのまま利益率に直結する新しい競争領域です。最強のモデルを選べる時代だからこそ、あえて選ばない判断にこそ価値が宿る。モデル選びは、性能比較からコスト設計へ。

text:
i kept watching solo founders win on x while doing way less of the busywork. so i broke down exactly how they pull it off.

it isn't discipline. they don't grind demo videos, og images, reels, a newsletter, a blog, and a posting schedule by hand. they build one system that makes all of it, and aim it at one channel.

here's how to build each piece:

1. build a loop, not a checklist.

four stages, four folders: ideas, draft, publish, learn.
- ideas: a running file the system keeps filling from what's already working in your niche
- voice: reverse-engineer your own 10 best posts into a traits file. sentence length, how you open, what you never do
- draft: one prompt that loads the voice file plus a single idea
- learn: log what got bookmarked, feed that back into which ideas get picked next

every surface (x, blog, newsletter) is just a different publish target hanging off the same drafted piece. build the loop once, not the chores forever.

2. chain specialists. stop one-shotting it.

five prompt files, one job each:
- strategist: topic + audience in, angle + hook + brief out
- researcher: brief in, sources + facts + 3 contrarian points out
- writer: brief + research in, full draft out
- editor: cuts 30%, sharpens the opening, rewrites the close
- publisher: formats for the target platform

output of one becomes input to the next. it beats a single chat for a concrete reason: an editor in a fresh window will actually cut what a writer "worked hard on." same window, it won't, because it watched the writer struggle. you touch it twice. two paragraphs in, approve at the end.

3. build the faceless video factory, then give it a brain.

the pipeline is script, voice, assembly, post, measure.
- claude writes the script. pick the niche by rpm and competition gap, not by what you personally like
- elevenlabs voices it
- capcut or any auto-editor assembles the clips or the slideshow
- a scheduler api drops it in as a draft so you can add trending audio before it publishes

the step everyone skips is the one that pays. wire the agent to read the funnel: views, then installs, then subscribers. it logs every hook's result and rewrites its own rules over time. an agent that just posts is noise. an agent that reads the funnel is distribution.

4. aim the whole machine at one channel: the one where your product is the audience.

before you automate anything, answer one question. where does my buyer already sit, and is my product about that place?

build a tool for x creators, sell it on x. the audience is pre-qualified, so even a post with 8 likes brings real leads.

the mistake is spreading across five platforms on day one and ending up with five weak channels. point everything at the single tightest product-to-audience fit. saturate it. expand only after it's working.

5. start the blog on day one, and write for your competitors' tools too.

this is the channel that compounds while you sleep.
- target the exact queries people type when they already have the problem. "where are X stored", "how to install Y"
- one article per query, and make every heading a question
- put a 40 to 60 word answer block at the very top. that block is what chatgpt and perplexity pull and cite
- add schema markup on every page (article, faq, howto)
- write guides for adjacent and competitor tools you don't even make. those queries have almost no competition

start before the product is finished. seo's clock starts at article one, so the earlier you begin the bigger the head start.

one catch. the system makes the content. it does not make the replies.

the fastest growth i found still came down to someone treating replies like a full-time job. short sessions through the day, real conversations, not broadcasts. automate the machine. you're still the one who talks to people.

so: which one channel are you going all in on, and what's the first surface you automate to feed it? specific moves only.

text:
Anthropicは最先端AI「Fable 5」の一般提供を今週再開へ、
一方、OpenAIは「GPT-5.6」を発表し、ここには3つのモデル：フラッグシップモデルの「Sol」、日常業務向けのバランスの取れたモデル「Terra」、高速で価格を抑えた「Luna」がある。
しかし「米国政府の要請」により、限定プレビューとして公開。「一般公開に向けて、政府と協力して最速で進める」(サム・アルトマンCEO)としている。

■使い分けは、こうです。
- Claude（アンスロピック社）= 賢さで勝負タイプ
難しい仕事を高い精度でこなす「優等生」。ただし料金は高め。
- OpenAI（GPT-5.6）= コスパで勝負タイプ
同じくらいの答えを、より少ない手間（＝少ないコスト）で出す「効率屋」。料金も安め。

つまり「とにかく一番賢いのがいいならClaude」「安くたくさん使いたいならOpenAI」という棲み分けができている。

---
そもそも今回、何が起きたのか
2026年6月、2つの会社がほぼ同時に最新AIを発表した。
- OpenAIは「GPT-5.6」を発表。中身は3種類に分かれています。
  - Sol（ソル）…一番賢い最上位モデル
  - Terra（テラ）…日常業務向けのバランス型（前モデル並みの性能で、お値段は半額）
  - Luna（ルナ）…とにかく速くて安い軽量モデル
- Anthropicは「Fable 5（フェイブル5）」、これまでで最も賢い一般向けモデルを出した。
さらに上の特別版「Mythos 5（ミュトス5）」もあり、政府公認の防御専門家など、ごく一部に制限されている。

両社とも「強すぎて、すぐには誰でも使えない」状況にある。アメリカ政府が「危ないかもしれないから、まず審査させて」と関与している。
- OpenAIは一部の信頼できる会社（約20社）に限定公開
- アンスロピックは輸出規制でいったん提供停止→順次再開中
といったAIが「兵器なみに規制される時代」を象徴する展開になっている。

---
■ここで、性能のくらべ方を、3つの観点で比べてみた。

AIの性能は「テスト（ベンチマーク）」の点数で比較できる。
●① プログラミング（コードを書く力）
- 「ターミナル操作」のテストでは：
  - OpenAIのSol（一番頑張るモードで）が 91.9点でトップ
  - Claudeの最上位Mythos 5が 88点、Fable 5が 84.3点
  → このテストではOpenAIがやや勝ち

- 「難しい開発作業」のテストでは：
  - ClaudeのFable 5が 80.3点、対するOpenAIの前モデルは 58.6点
  →Claudeが圧勝
- 実例：ある決済会社（Stripe）では、人が手作業で2か月かかる大規模な改修を、Claudeが1日で終わらせた。

text:
𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐬

Probably the biggest topic the past two weeks have been the takedown and usage of Anthropic’s Fable 5 AI model.

Every AI creator has spoken about how its been banned in and outside of the country due to “security” concerns by the government.

People got depressed.

Even Theo (of T3 chat) who is reputedly “Anthropics #1 hater” subscribed to two Claude Max accounts just to use Fable when it was out.

Because Fable was genuinely good.

Now, its gone.

But then came https://t.co/x0J9hgvlrt, who released the latest in their flagship GLM model, GLM 5.2.

An open weight model that in many people’s opinions (including myself) performs much better in actual real life tasks than Opus 4.8.

GLM 5.2 was - and is - very well received by everyone.

People applauded how far open source has come in catching up to the big boys.

For a moment, there was morale.

Then morale came crashing back down again because OpenAI wanted to release GPT 5.6 which is reportedly 𝑒𝑣𝑒𝑛 𝑏𝑒𝑡𝑡𝑒𝑟 than Fable 5.

But they can’t because, well, 𝑠𝑒𝑐𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑠.

So Anthropic has not only gotten their models become exclusive, now they’ve have - once again - forced everyone to follow their lead.

Including making their #1 rival’s newest best model banned.

The space is rife with opinions.

- “Anthropic has been asking for government regulation, so now they got it! Serves them right!”
- “This isn’t actually a security thing, this is just an excuse to suppress people!”
- “The tech bros are looking to control WHO gets the tech - look, only a FEW companies gets the model!”

Just thinking about this makes me mad.

I like Anthropic’s models.

But I don’t like Anthropic.

More specifically, the kinds of practices that they do.

And I fear what this means to the rest of us if more and more of these practices become commonplace.

I’ve been saying for some time now that the age of AI subsidy is coming to an end.

That people should be taking advantage of this moment to build for when all this is over, when the latest models are exclusive only to a select few.

But my warnings have fallen on deaf ears and people are still going around doing what they do, the way they’ve always done it (without AI).

And now, more proof is coming out on how big tech is going to play this.

- First, they made you fall in love with their products.
- Second, they get you so dependent on their products, that it is too costly to leave.
- Third, they introduce more powerful and expensive models (2-3x more expensive).
- Fourth, they quietly make their older models - the one you’re used to - dumber.
- Fifth, they pull stunts like these to hype things up, raise share prices, and make their best models only available to a select few, making the government throw regulations to limit it even further.
- Finally, they deprecate older models entirely so you are either stuck paying only premium, or stuck with bad models that can’t do a fraction of what the premium ones can do.

This is why so many people are mad.

Big tech is moving the world around like chess pieces, and the public don’t seem to know or care to learn.

- Grok 4.3 (v8 기반, 0.5T 모델)은 작년 12월에 학습이 끝났지만 기반이 약했음
- Cursor의 데이터와 엔지니어들이 v9 포스트트레이닝에 통합됨
- 8월에 **2T 규모**의 대형 학습이 예정됨

---

### 2. Fable 5와 GPT-5.6 공개 임박

- **Fable 5**와 **GPT-5.6**이 다음 주에 일반 공개될 가능성이 높음 (해외 포함)
- 지금까지의 지연으로 해외 연구소들이 한 달간 증류(distillation) 기회를 잃음
- 모델 지문(fingerprinting)이 가능할 정도로 프론티어 모델이 “새는(leaky)” 상태

### 3. 중국 오픈소스 모델의 급성장

- **GLM-5.2**를 “오픈소스 Claude 모먼트”라고 평가

- Ethan Mollick의 새로운 벤치마크: 미국과 중국 오픈 모델 간 격차가 **3개월** 수준으로 좁혀짐

### 4. 빅테크의 방어 움직임

- Meta가 엔지니어들의 **Claude Code**와 **Codex** 사용을 제한

- MetaCode를 자체적으로 구축 중

---

### 5. 주권(Sovereignty)과 규제

- Palantir + NVIDIA: 공군 기밀 환경(air-gapped)에서 Nemotron 오픈 모델을 운영할 수 있는 엔진 제공
- 오스트리아: EU 내에 Anthropic을 유치하려는 움직임
- 캘리포니아: 모든 주정부 기관에 Claude를 50% 할인 + 무료 교육 제공
- Mark Warner 상원의원: AI 서비스에 “충성 의무(duty of loyalty)”를 부과하는 법안 추진

---

### 6. 하드웨어와 인프라

- 메모리 공급 부족이 2027년까지 지속될 전망 (데이터센터 수요 때문)
- 한국: **5850억 달러** 규모 반도체 메가컴플렉스 추진
- 빅5 연구소들이 아직 세계 AI 컴퓨트의 절반도 사용하지 않았지만, Anthropic과 OpenAI가 빠르게 흡수할 가능성
- 인도네시아에 대규모 Nvidia 캠퍼스 건설 (최대 300억 달러 규모)

---

### 7. 조직과 문화 변화

- Claude Code 개발자(Boris Cherny): 엔지니어링·제품·디자인이 5가지 archetype(프로토타이퍼, 빌더, 스위퍼, 그로워, 메인테이너)으로 재편될 것이라고 전망
- AI 코딩 비용이 2028년에는 개발자 연봉을 넘어설 전망
- 애니메이션 스튜디오: AI 활용으로 제작비를 기존의 1/7~1/13 수준으로 낮추는 계획
- GPT-5.6 Pro가 31분 만에 법적으로 구별되는 포켓몬 클론 게임을 생성

---

### 8. 신뢰와 진위성 문제

- 시험 부정행위 증가 (스마트 안경으로 답안 확인)
- AI 진단을 의사 진단보다 신뢰하는 사례 증가
- Tidal: 7월 중순부터 완전 AI 생성 음악에 태그를 붙이고 로열티를 대폭 삭감

---

### 9. 경제 변화

- Rocket Lab이 Iridium을 약 **80억 달러**에 인수 (우주 스택 전체 소유 목적)
- Magnificent 7의 P/E 프리미엄이 10년 만에 최저 수준으로 하락
- 대도시에서 임대가 구매보다 저렴해지면서 “소유의 의미”에 대한 의문 증가
- GLP-1 약물(위고비 등) 수요 폭증으로 **유청 단백질(whey)** 공급 부족 심화

**마지막 문장**: “Where there's a will, there's a whey.” (의지가 있는 곳에 길이 있다 → whey(유청)로 말장난)

---

### 종합 한 줄 요약

**2026년 6월 29일 현재**, Grok v9과 Fable 5 / GPT-5.6의 공개가 임박하면서 프론티어 모델 경쟁이 다시 가열되고 있으며, 동시에 중국 오픈소스 모델(GLM-5.2 등)의 급성장과 미국 빅테크의 방어 움직임, 그리고 AI로 인한 조직·문화·경제 재편이 동시에 진행되고 있습니다.

Devin Fusion ชี้ทิศทางใหม่ AI Coding: แข่งกันจัดทีม AI ไม่ใช่แข่งกันสร้างโมเดล

ในช่วงสองปีที่ผ่านมา การแข่งขันของ AI Coding Agent มุ่งไปที่คำถามว่า โมเดลใดเขียนโค้ดได้ดีที่สุด บริษัทต่าง ๆ พยายามนำโมเดลระดับ Frontier เข้ามาเป็นหัวใจของระบบ ไม่ว่าจะเป็น Claude, GPT หรือโมเดลรุ่นใหม่ที่มีความสามารถสูงขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ แต่เมื่อความสามารถของโมเดลเพิ่มขึ้น ต้นทุนในการใช้งานก็เพิ่มขึ้นตาม และเริ่มกลายเป็นข้อจำกัดสำคัญสำหรับการนำ AI Agent ไปใช้งานในวงกว้าง

การเปิดตัว Devin Fusion ของ Cognition Labs จึงน่าสนใจ เพราะบริษัทไม่ได้พยายามสร้างโมเดลใหม่ที่ฉลาดกว่าเดิม หากแต่กำลังตั้งคำถามกับสมมติฐานเดิมของวงการว่า จำเป็นหรือไม่ที่ทุกขั้นตอนของการเขียนโปรแกรมจะต้องใช้โมเดลราคาแพงที่สุด

Cognition ระบุว่าแนวทางการทำ Model Routing แบบดั้งเดิม แม้จะทำคะแนน Benchmark ได้ดี แต่กลับไม่สะท้อนประสบการณ์การพัฒนาซอฟต์แวร์จริง เพราะงานเขียนโค้ดไม่ได้วัดเพียงว่า "ทำสำเร็จหรือไม่" แต่ยังรวมถึงคุณภาพของโค้ด ความสม่ำเสมอของสไตล์ ความสามารถในการรีวิว และความพร้อมที่จะนำโค้ดไปรวมเข้ากับระบบจริง (merge) ซึ่งเป็นสิ่งที่ Benchmark แบบผ่านหรือไม่ผ่านเพียงอย่างเดียวไม่สามารถวัดได้

แนวคิดของ Devin Fusion จึงเปลี่ยนจากการเลือกโมเดลเพียงตัวเดียว มาเป็นการสร้าง ระบบที่ให้หลายโมเดลทำงานร่วมกัน โดยแบ่งบทบาทตามความเหมาะสม โมเดลหลักรับหน้าที่วางแผน วิเคราะห์ และตรวจสอบภาพรวม ขณะที่โมเดลต้นทุนต่ำทำหน้าที่เป็น Sidekick สำหรับงานที่เป็นกิจวัตร เช่น การรันเทสต์ การตรวจ lint การแก้ไขโค้ดเล็ก ๆ หรือการจัดการงานซ้ำ ๆ ที่ไม่จำเป็นต้องใช้เหตุผลระดับสูง

จุดที่แตกต่างจากระบบ Routing ทั่วไปคือ Mid-Session Routing ซึ่งเปิดโอกาสให้ Agent เปลี่ยนโมเดลระหว่างการทำงานได้ เมื่อพบว่าความซับซ้อนของงานเปลี่ยนไป เพราะในโลกของการพัฒนาซอฟต์แวร์ คำสั่งง่าย ๆ อย่าง "แก้บั๊กนี้" อาจจบลงด้วยการแก้ไขเพียงหนึ่งบรรทัด หรืออาจกลายเป็นการปรับสถาปัตยกรรมทั้งระบบก็ได้ ความยากของงานจึงไม่สามารถตัดสินได้จาก Prompt ตั้งแต่ต้น แต่ต้องอาศัยการสำรวจฐานโค้ดและการวิเคราะห์ระหว่างการทำงาน

แนวทางนี้สะท้อนการเปลี่ยนแปลงที่กำลังเกิดขึ้นในวงการ Agentic AI กล่าวคือ AI Agent ไม่ได้ถูกออกแบบให้เป็นผู้เชี่ยวชาญเพียงคนเดียวอีกต่อไป แต่เริ่มมีลักษณะคล้ายทีมวิศวกรที่แบ่งหน้าที่กันทำงาน บางโมเดลเชี่ยวชาญด้านการวางแผน บางโมเดลเชี่ยวชาญด้านการดำเนินงาน และบางโมเดลทำหน้าที่ตรวจสอบคุณภาพ ก่อนจะรวมผลลัพธ์กลับมาเป็นคำตอบเดียวให้ผู้ใช้

text:
The Gate and the Download

The export order that pulled @AnthropicAI 's models off the market was meant to keep a dangerous capability out of foreign hands. One day later, that capability arrived as a free download.

On June 12, the Commerce Dep. forced Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 worldwide, citing the risk that their cybersecurity powers could reach adversaries. On June 13, the Chinese lab @ZhipuAI released GLM-5.2, an open-weight model anyone on Earth can download, run, and modify. Security researchers now say it matches the restricted American models at the one task that justified the ban: finding software vulnerabilities. The thing the gate was built to contain walked through the wall beside it the next morning.

This is the structural fact the week delivered. An export control can only touch what the U.S. controls, which is access to a closed model sitting behind an American API. It does nothing to a set of open weights already copied onto hard drives in dozens of countries. You can switch off a model you host. You cannot un-download one that someone else gave away. The policy removed the most capable American option from the shelf and, in the same motion, made the Chinese substitute the obvious default.

And the substitute is cheap. GLM-5.2 runs at roughly a sixth the cost of Claude Opus 4.8 on the output tokens that dominate real workloads. By May, open-weight Chinese models already accounted for around 61% of all tokens consumed on one of the largest model routers, with four of the five most-used models built in China. The ban did not just fail to contain a capability. It handed a price advantage to the exact alternative it was trying to outrun, at the moment cost-sensitive buyers were already migrating.

The criticism is no longer coming from one corner. Saif Khan, who worked on export restrictions under Biden, called banning Fable while selling China the chips to build its own version a gift to Beijing. @NielsProvos , who led security at @Google and @stripe , said the policy incentivizes the world to adopt cheaper Chinese open models while undermining the US industry, and added simply, I don't understand it. And @DavidSacks , the administration's own AI czar, used the news to warn that America wins by being pro-innovation and pro-export, and deviates from that at its peril. Export hawks, security researchers, and the White House AI lead rarely agree on anything. They have converged against the same policy.

Honesty requires holding the other half. The parity claim is narrower than the headline. @semgrep , whose test produced the result, stressed it was one dataset, one run, one task, and that its own purpose-built tooling still beats every raw model. GLM-5.2 wins the narrow security benchmark and loses the harder reasoning tasks to American systems. And there is a shadow over how it got so good so fast: researchers flagged that its outputs correlate unusually closely with @claudeai and @OpenAI GPT, raising the same distillation question that has Anthropic accusing Alibaba of harvesting its model. The Chinese capability may be real, partly borrowed, and overstated all at once. 

But the direction does not depend on the exact benchmark. Strip away the cyberwarfare framing and what remains is a lesson about the shape of control. A gate works only on what must pass through it. The American labs and their government built an architecture of permission, the approval to ship, the letter that switches a model off, the tier the state sets. That architecture governs the closed layer beautifully and the open layer not at all. Every restriction on the gated American model is an advertisement for the ungated Chinese one. The harder Washington holds the door, the more the traffic routes around it.

This is the cost of treating capability as something you can lock in a vault. The vault works until someone gives the same thing away for free, and then the vault is just a sign that says the good stuff is somewhere else.

text:
Alarma en Washington: El nuevo modelo open-weight GLM-5.2 de Zhipu AI empata con Claude Mythos cazando vulnerabilidades. 🇨🇳🔓🛡️

La brecha entre la IA propietaria de EE. UU. y el código abierto chino se acaba de cerrar en el sector más crítico: la ciberseguridad. Un informe de The Wall Street Journal e investigaciones independientes revelan que GLM-5.2 (de la startup Zhipu AI / Z . ai) alcanza capacidades de frontera para detectar fallos de software.  

Los datos que sacuden a la industria:

- Victoria en benchmarks: En pruebas independientes de la firma Semgrep para detectar vulnerabilidades críticas de autorización (IDOR), GLM-5.2 logró un 39% de precisión (F1) en un entorno básico. Superó el 32% de Claude Code y a Claude Opus 4.8, e igualó el rendimiento de Claude Mythos si se le añade un prompt estructurado.  

- Un sexto del costo: Mientras que cazar un bug con el ecosistema cerrado de Anthropic cuesta más de $1.00 en tokens, el modelo de Zhipu lo hace por apenas $0.17 por vulnerabilidad. Su arquitectura de 753B parámetros y ventana de 1M de contexto está hiperoptimizada para la persistencia en agentes de código.  

- El dilema de seguridad: A diferencia de Mythos o GPT-5.6 (fuertemente restringidos y vigilados por la administración Trump), GLM-5.2 es un modelo open-weight de libre descarga global. Puede ejecutarse localmente, modificarse y eliminársele cualquier guardrail ético.  

El golpe desafía la premisa de la Casa Blanca de que los controles de exportación de hardware frenarían el desarrollo de armas cibernéticas autónomas en el extranjero. La carrera ya no es solo por el modelo más grande, sino por quién democratiza primero el software de ataque y defensa.

author: curiouspenguin
text:
$claude, $anthropic The CA–Anthropic deal reads like a SaaS discount story. It isn't. It's Anthropic's first visible step from model layer → orchestration layer in 2B2G — and that's where durable rent actually lives.

The model layer is the shortest-duration moat in AI: frontier leads get matched in quarters. Real durability comes from converting a fleeting model lead into switching costs before the lead erodes.

Watch the structure: a shared-services procurement portal (SITeS), 50% discount, and a state-built orchestration shell (Poppy). Surface-read: buyer guarding against vendor lock-in. But weak public buyers can't actually build or maintain orchestration alone — which turns "buyer-built" into a Forward-Deployed-Engineer entry point, not a defense. This is the Palantir playbook's opening move.

The prize isn't the smartest model. It's welding Claude into low-digitization, high-red-tape government systems. That switching cost is rooted in org inertia + political accountability, NOT technology — so it survives the one thing that dissolves ordinary integration moats: models getting good enough to integrate themselves.

Key tension to track: the same frontier capability that pries open these systems is also what can detonate Anthropic's longest-duration asset — trust/compliance access (see Mythos/Fable suspension). Capability opens the window; safety positioning is what they bank during it.

Not investable directly (still private). But it reprices the whole 2B2G AI stack — and tells you which layer to underwrite when it is. Watch FDE-type hiring and contract language shifting from "subscription" to "custom deployment."

author: stretchcloud
text:
The bottleneck in agentic coding just moved from the model to the harness.

Cognition shipped Devin Fusion today. The mechanism is not model routing. Not picking one model for the entire task. A sidekick architecture: a frontier model runs the session, both models maintain their own cached context, and the frontier model decides what to delegate in real time. Handoffs happen during context compaction, avoiding cache misses entirely.

The numbers on FrontierCode Extended: Fusion plus Fable 5 matches pure Fable 5 performance at 41% lower cost. Without Fable 5, suspended since June 12 per a US government export control directive, Fusion matches Opus and GPT-5.5 at 35% lower cost. 88% of Cognition's internal merged PRs ran through the automated router with no human override.

The task breakdown reveals the actual rule. Mechanical work delegates cleanly: lint fixes, test runs, rote refactors. One javascript refactor delegated the slow test suite and cut cost 62% at no quality loss. Judgment-heavy work backfires. A TypeScript feature with subtle intent requirements scored 27 via sidekick versus 54 solo. The sidekick needs to know what it cannot do.

Harness engineering research this spring shows evolved scaffolds cut token usage by 12% on SWE-bench Verified without changing the base model. Claude Opus 4.8 sits at 88.6% on SWE-bench Verified. Devin's PR merge rate is 67%, up from 34% a year ago. The gains are coming from harness improvements, not just raw model capability.

The frame I keep returning to: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codeium, Claude Code, and Devin are all building proprietary scaffolds on top of the same frontier APIs. Fable 5 inside the Fusion harness scored 57.6 on FrontierCode. Opus 4.8 alone scored 48.8 at higher cost. The model is a commodity input. The harness is the product.

https://t.co/gdvHhnLqLl
